name: Toyota Camry
engine: 2.5L naturally-aspirated I4 (A25A-FKS), 203 hp (206 on XSE) — 3.5L V6 (2GR-FKS), 301 hp — 2.5L hybrid, 208 hp combined
drivetrain: FWD · available AWD on the 2.5L I4 (added for 2020)
reliability: 9/10 — the XV70 Camry is one of the most dependable midsize sedans on the road. The 2.5L Dynamic Force four, the 2GR V6, and the hybrid system are all proven, long-lived powertrains, and the 8-speed automatic settled down after some early-2018 low-speed hesitation. The notable recall is the 2020 Denso low-pressure fuel pump, which affected many brands. Buy one with maintenance records and it will go the distance.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Average · Maintenance ~$400/yr · Very strong resale · The hybrid's real-world 45–50 mpg makes it one of the cheapest ways to cover big miles in comfort
popular_mods: A second set of wheels with winter tires for cold-climate owners
All-weather floor liners and quality all-season tires
Tasteful wheel/tire upgrades — the TRD trim shows the sportier direction owners like
Sound-deadening and OEM-plus dampers on higher-mileage cars for a quieter, tighter ride
Honest take: the V6 XSE/TRD is genuinely quick, but the hybrid is the smart-money Camry — spend on maintenance, not power
oil_type: 0W-16 full synthetic (0W-20 acceptable on the V6 — check the cap)

generations.7th Gen XV50 (2012–2017 US): The value-and-space Camry — 2.5L four or the 268 hp 3.5L V6, 6-speed automatic. Comfortable and famously durable if a little anonymous to drive.
generations.8th Gen XV70 (2018–2024 US): A sharper, better-looking redesign on the TNGA-K platform — 203 hp 2.5L four, an available 301 hp V6, an efficient hybrid, and (from 2020) available AWD on the four. Toyota Safety Sense standard.
generations.9th Gen (2025+ US): Went hybrid-only with a standard AWD option, dropping the V6 entirely in favor of efficiency.

common_issues: 2020 Denso low-pressure fuel-pump recall — industry-wide; confirm it is closed by VIN on 2018–2020 cars
Some early 2018 cars showed low-speed 8-speed automatic hesitation/harshness — improved with software
More road and tire noise than a luxury sedan, especially on the sportier trims with bigger wheels
Infotainment on early XV70 cars felt dated; later years added wireless CarPlay/Android Auto
V6 and 2.0T-style power is fun but the V6 asks for a bit more fuel — the four and hybrid are the frugal picks
maintenance_tips: Keep up with the specified synthetic oil on the Maintenance Minder
Service the 8-speed automatic fluid on schedule despite 'lifetime' claims — cheap insurance
Confirm the fuel-pump recall and any open recalls by VIN
On the hybrid, keep the 12V battery healthy and the traction battery cooling intake (behind the rear seat) clean
Budget for brakes and tires on the heavier V6/AWD cars; otherwise upkeep is minimal
